*Topics — What a work is about. **Moral psychology** — morality as a natural phenomenon — moral judgement, emotion and norms, and their evolution, development and variation across cultures; descriptive, where ethics is normative (group: philosophy; ADR-018).

| [THEORY-121](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-121.md) v7 | Guidance control suffices for responsibility | Fischer and Ravizza, in their own précis ([LIT-728](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-728.md), read): moral responsibility requires guidance control, not regulative control over alternatives. Guidance control is acting from a mechanism one has made one's own by taking responsibility for it, which is moderately reasons-responsive: regularly receptive to reasons, some moral, and at least weakly reactive. Fischer's 1987 paper ([LIT-687](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-687.md), read) is the weak-responsiveness origin. The view is compatible with causal determinism. | Active |
| [THEORY-122](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-122.md) v2 | Responsibility needs normative competence | Susan Wolf's Reason View, reported second-hand: the primary texts are unread. McKenna and Coates ([LIT-291](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-291.md), §4.3) report that for Wolf free will is the ability to act in accord with the True and the Good, an anchor outside the agent's psychology. Talbert ([LIT-691](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-691.md), §§3.1.1, 3.2) reports her case against deep-self or Real Self views and the JoJo case: JoJo identifies wholly with the cruel values his father raised him in, yet is not responsible, because he cannot appreciate that they are wrong. The claim is a necessary condition. It does not by itself say whether the ability must include being able to do otherwise; that is [THEORY-118](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-118.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-147](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-147.md) v3 | Attributability and accountability are independent | Wolf (2015), [LIT-747](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-747.md), the 2013 Routledge Lecture. We are deeply, not merely causally, responsible for nonmoral traits and art, by the self-disclosure view. Watson's two-level view, accountability as attributability plus control, is rejected: a stipulated psychopath may be accountable for acts whose source is not attributable to him. Fitness for reactive attitudes is, on Wolf's hunch, being an intelligent self. Proposed: the positive view is her hunch. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-435](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-435.md) | Care and Fairness are endorsed across politics | Graham, Haidt et al. | [THEORY-457](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-457.md) | Partner choice selects proportional fairness | Baumard, André & Sperber (2013), [LIT-508](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-508.md), read in [NOTE-407](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-407.md), with its 28 commentaries and Response. The authors disagree among themselves about whether purity, loyalty and kin care are moral at all. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-468](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-468.md) | Morality is solutions to cooperation problems | Curry (2016), [LIT-503](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-503.md), read in [NOTE-408](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-408.md), with its two tests, [LIT-047](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-047.md) ([NOTE-034](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-034.md)) and [LIT-496](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-496.md) ([NOTE-412](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-412.md)). The positive half has support: the seven are described as good wherever ethnographers record them, and questionnaire items for them form seven factors. The negative half, that nothing else is moralized, is the theory's own stated prediction (p. 40). No study in the programme has tested it blind, and where non-cooperative items appear, the programme's own data show them moralized. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-494](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-494.md) | Puritanism is cooperative morality | Fitouchi, André & Baumard (2021), [LIT-101](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-101.md), read in [NOTE-132](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-132.md). In the authors' vignette studies (N > 1,100), perceived loss of self-control mediated all of the perceived effect of indulgence on cooperativeness. The rest is a review: disgust does not amplify condemnation once harm is controlled, and a society's valuing of self-control predicts its hygiene norms better than pathogen threat. The account is agnostic about whether the norms work, excludes contamination purity by definition, and has shown that people hold the belief, not that the belief made the norms. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-495](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-495.md) | Obligation is internalized joint-agent pressure | Tomasello (2019), [LIT-125](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-125.md), read in [NOTE-185](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-185.md). A synthesis of developmental and comparative experiments, mostly from the author's lab, on WEIRD children and chimpanzees; no new data. The behavioural contrasts between committed and side-by-side play are moderately supported. That they reflect felt obligation, rather than prosociality or learned scripts, is argued, not shown. It explains the sense of obligation, not what anyone is obliged to do, as the author concedes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-505](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-505.md) | Cooperation domains factor only by relevance | Curry, Jones Chesters & Van Lissa (2019), [LIT-496](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-496.md), read in [NOTE-412](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-412.md), and the independent Turkish validation by Yilmaz, Harma & Doğruyol (2021), [LIT-513](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-513.md) ([NOTE-397](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-397.md)). Relevance items fit seven factors in all three samples (CFI .98 UK, .95 Turkey). Judgement items do not (CFI .87, .83), and a seven-domain model of both fails (CFI .73, .75). The items were written from the theory and selected for fit within each domain, several subscales correlate above .8, and no item is non-cooperative. This is evidence about the instrument's structure, not about what morality contains. | Active |

| [THEORY-558](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-558.md) | Moral judgment is intuition; reasoning post hoc | Haidt (2001), [LIT-511](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-511.md), read in [NOTE-403](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-403.md): the social intuitionist model. Its case rests mostly on non-moral evidence about automaticity, motivated reasoning and confabulation, carried over by argument. Its direct moral evidence is that harmless taboo violations are condemned and that affect predicts the condemnation better than perceived harm. | [THEORY-613](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-613.md) | MFQ-2's six foundations fit across 19 nations | Atari, Haidt, Graham, Koleva, Stevens & Dehghani (2023), [LIT-500](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-500.md), read in [NOTE-398](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-398.md). 36 items, developed in 25 populations, fit six factors in 19 nations (ESEM CFI .979). | [THEORY-626](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-626.md) | Moral judgment depends on relational model | Rai & Fiske (2011), [LIT-507](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-507.md), read in [NOTE-405](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-405.md). A theoretical review with no new data. Its strongest support is cited work on relational framing and on morally motivated violence. | [THEORY-632](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-632.md) | Purity is moralized, against cooperation theory | Curry, Jones Chesters & Van Lissa (2019), [LIT-496](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-496.md), read in [NOTE-412](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-412.md), against the prediction stated in Curry (2016), [LIT-503](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-503.md) ([NOTE-408](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-408.md)), with the harmless-wrongs studies Haidt (2001) reports, [LIT-511](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-511.md) ([NOTE-403](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-403.md)). In two samples, MFQ purity items are rated morally relevant at the level of ingroup and authority items, and the authors concede this "appear[s] to contradict" the theory. | [THEORY-653](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-653.md) | Cooperation is praised everywhere, weakly tested | Curry, Mullins & Whitehouse (2019), [LIT-047](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-047.md), read in [NOTE-034](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-034.md). Coding eHRAF paragraphs on the 60 Probability Sample societies found 962 morally valenced mentions of helping kin, helping one's group, reciprocating, bravery, deference, dividing disputed resources and respecting possession; 961 were positive. Presence ran from property (54/60) to fairness (9/60) and tracked ethnographic coverage (r = .43). The behaviours are defined in virtue terms and conflicts were set aside, so a negative was nearly impossible to code. It is a description of the coded record, not a test of whether morality is only about cooperation. | Active |
| [THEORY-663](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-663.md) | Reciprocal altruism can evolve between non-kin | Trivers (1971), [LIT-510](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-510.md), read in full in [NOTE-402](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-402.md). A verbal model, with a Prisoner's Dilemma sketch Hamilton communicated, followed by a functional account of the human emotions that would regulate reciprocity. The model is plausible and was later formalized. The psychology is fitted to 1960s social-psychology findings, mostly on American students, and the heritability of the dispositions is assumed. Trivers knows "of no psychological studies on the detection of sham moralistic aggression and sham guilt" (p. 51). His "unfairness" is inequity in exchange, not the division of a disputed resource. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-892](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-892.md) v2 | Psychopathy is one dimension, not a type | Hare and Neumann (2008), read in [NOTE-1094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1094.md). The PCL-R's twenty items load on four correlated factors, which pair into Factor 1 (interpersonal, affective) and Factor 2 (lifestyle, antisocial) and are explained by one superordinate factor. The affective features are tied to the antisocial ones, so the authors deny that any component is the disorder's core, and they read the evidence as dimensional. Filed for the record's question on corporate psychopathy, which asks which of these features could be said of a corporation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1352](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1352.md) v2 | Cooperation holds in dyads, frays between groups | Van Lange and Bergmann (2026), [LIT-2002](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2002.md), read in [NOTE-1537](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1537.md).
